meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain — unitary national jurisdiction (no sub-state registry, tax or incorporation distinction applicable to the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European; codified mercantile and registry law under the Código de Comercio, Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 Ley de Sociedades de Capital, and Real Decreto 1784/1996 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 14 November 2005; in force 1 July 2007)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated 2020; ratification pending as of the assessment date)

Spain–Argentina Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (AAPPE, 1991); Spain–Mexico AAPPE (1995); Spain–Chile AAPPE (1993); Spain–Colombia AAPPE (1995); Spain–Peru AAPPE (2003); Spain–Uruguay AAPPE (1992)
Spain–China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 1992) and Spain–China social security agreement
Bilateral double-taxation conventions between Spain and more than 90 jurisdictions, including Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela
EU internal market treaties (TFEU), EU–Mexico and EU–Chile Association Agreements, and the EU–Mercosur Association Agreement (political agreement reached in December 2024; entry into force pending)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 4, 11, 14-15, 25 and 31); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010, as amended; Ley 6/2023, de 22 de junio, amending Law 10/2010 in transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended, and the EU AML/CFT package, including Regulation (EU) 2024/1624; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), arts. 23 and 38; Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 405-410; operational rules of the Registro de Titularidades Reales (UBO register) administered by the Colegio de Registradores de España.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal — the Registro de Titularidades Reales is accessible to competent supervisory authorities, notaries, mercantile registrars, and obliged entities performing customer due diligence upon demonstration of a legitimate interest; general public access remains restricted following the judgment of the Court of Justice of the European Union of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20) and its domestic implementation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory certificate of incorporation or registry extract of each non-resident corporate shareholder (certificado de registro mercantil de origen)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, commercial register or equivalent authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Certificate under the Hague Apostille Convention 1961; where the state of origin is not a party to the Convention, full consular legalization through the Spanish diplomatic mission, followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney and corporate authorization for the incorporator(s) and initial directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or equivalent certification authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Spanish consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into Spanish (traducción jurada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports or national identity documents of all ultimate beneficial owners and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry, notary or accredited certification body in the country of origin; alternatively certification at a Spanish consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the notarial verification page, plus sworn Spanish translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or legal existence (certificado de vigencia) for each corporate shareholder, issued not earlier than the certificate date
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or duly accredited legal representative in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence under Law 10/2010, arts. 14-15; compulsory screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against Spanish national sanctions lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, and United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, conducted before deed execution and repeated at each material review event; PEP identification covers domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, family members and close associates, with a mandatory 12-month post-cessation cooling-off period or documented lower-risk justification; screening evidence and CDD records must be preserved for at least ten years pursuant to Law 10/2010, art. 25.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) — telematic application 'Oficina Virtual del Registro Mercantil Central' operated by the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.rmc.es / www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate denomination must be expressed in Spanish or in any co-official language of Spain (Catalan/Valencian, Galician or Basque); foreign-language expressions are admitted only where they are of current usage in Spanish commercial nomenclature, descriptive of the corporate purpose, and transcribed in Roman characters; the denomination must include the legal form 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.', and must not mislead as to the legal form, national or international scope, public character, or object of the company (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, arts. 405-410).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Sociedad Anónima', 'S.A.', 'S.A.U.' where the incorporated vehicle is an SL (misrepresentation of legal form; absolutely barred)
'Banco', 'Caja', 'Financiera', 'Aseguradora', 'Correduría' (financial-sector denominations requiring prior authorization from the Banco de España or the Dirección General de Seguros)
'Instituto', 'Ministerio', 'Gobierno', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Administración' (public-administration references barred under art. 407 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil)
'España', 'Nacional', 'Estatal' (restricted; require justification and prior approval of the competent registry authority)
'Internacional', 'Mundial', 'Global', 'UE', 'ONU', 'Europeo' (geographic or supranational scope tokens subject to substantive review and prior ministerial clearance)
'Pública', 'Público' where they mislead as to the public-law or hybrid nature of the entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registro Mercantil Central refuses or conditions a proposed denomination, the applicant may (1) resubmit up to five alternative denomination candidates through the RMC telematic service within the prevailing reservation window; (2) request a reasoned written certification of the rejection; and (3) file, within one month of notification, an optional reconsideration petition followed by a hierarchical administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice. The underlying negative name certificate issued by the RMC remains statutorily valid for three months, which is harmonized with the 30-day pipeline window by executing the notarial incorporation deed immediately upon clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a sole solution: an SL undertaking medical-device manufacturing (ISIC 3250, Regulation (EU) 2017/745) must maintain a genuine physical establishment in Spain; the registered office may be a professional office shared with administrative service providers only where (i) a verifiable physical registered-office address exists, (ii) the management and accounting substance of the SL is demonstrable, and (iii) the AEMPS economic-operator registration and ISO 13485 quality-management conformity assessment identify a real operational site for manufacturing, warehousing or quality control.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high quantified risk: approximately 45-60% cumulative probability of at least one announced or unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operations, driven principally by AEMPS and Notified-Body conformity audits under the Medical Device Regulation, supplemented by intermittent AEAT tax verification visits and sporadic Mercantile Registry supervision of registered-office reality.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): arts. 20-22 (escritura y constitución), arts. 23-28 (statutory contents, contributions and capital), arts. 9-11 (registered office), arts. 58-62 (administration), arts. 210-214 (appointment of administrators), arts. 132-138 (NIF and registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (central names registry) and the competent Registro Mercantil Provincial for the registered office; deed authenticated by a Spanish notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public incorporation deed), filed with the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid up before execution of the deed, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. Non-cash contributions must be valued by an independent expert and described in the deed. The bank funds remain segregated until the NIF is obtained and the company is registered; after registration, the administrators may release them.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the company is formally constituted under Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010. The shareholders approve the entire share capital: [SHAREHOLDER A], with NIE [NIE], subscribes and pays up EUR [AMOUNT]; [SHAREHOLDER B], with NIE [NIE], subscribes and pays up EUR [AMOUNT]. The registered office is fixed at [FULL ADDRESS], Spain. The first administrators are appointed: [DIRECTOR NAME] as Managing Director and [DIRECTOR NAME] as Secretary/Treasurer, with full corporate powers and joint signatures for bank accounts and contracts. This Board Resolution is effective immediately. The directors are expressly authorised to open bank accounts, execute documents, appear before notaries and public registries, and carry out all acts necessary to complete registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Spanish taxpayer and identity numbers for shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de la Policía / Oficina de Extranjería (for NIE) and Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Non-resident physical shareholders and directors must obtain a NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjeros) before signing the deed. Submit Form EX-15 at a Spanish consulate overseas or, if already in Spain, at a National Police Station with appointment. The NIE certificate must be attached to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID card
Completed Form EX-15
Proof of investment purpose (proposed company activity and capital)
Consular or police appointment confirmation
Criminal record certificate if requested for directorship roles
Medical/physical presence documentation if applying inside Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the documentation on the AEAT/police file within 10 business days; re-file the application. If refused for incorrect information, file a written reconsideration or an appeal with the administrative body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name and obtain negative name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name certificate application to the RMC for the proposed registered name of the SL. Use Form de denominación social or the self-service online procedure. Obtain a full searching of identical or misleading names; the RMC must not issue a certificate if the name is too close to an existing one. Usually processed within 3 business days. The certificate is valid for 3 months and must be attached to the deed.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
NIE/passport copies of the promoter/shareholders
Payment of 0 to EUR 24 depending on number of names requested
Certificate of identity and authority if representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC refuses due to similarity, present an alternative name within the same application or file a new name petition. If the refusal is based on incorrect grounds, file a formal request for revision with the RMC's certification division before initiation of other steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the notarial district where the registered office is domiciled
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft bylaws (estatutos), capital deposit certificate, name certificate, and identity documents. The notary will read the deed aloud, verify the identity and legal capacity of shareholders, and authenticate the deed. The deed must state the subscribed capital, means of payment, registered office, purpose, directors, and corporate governance rules. The notary then delivers an authenticated first copy for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate issued by RMC
Bank certificate confirming deposit of the full capital amount
NIE / DNI / passport of all shareholders and directors
Draft articles of association (estatutos) and shareholders' agreement (if any)
Statement of lawful purpose and planned ISIC/NAICS activities
Proof of non-cash contribution valuation if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to legal or formal defects, correct the deed draft and re-execute. If the notary identifies insufficient capital, obtain proper proof of full payment. Notarial refusal can be challenged by filing with the Mercantile Registry or court if the notary fails to justify under LSC arts. 22 and 25.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay transfer tax and obtain provisional NIF (CIF) for the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed, submit Form 036 to AEAT to assign a provisional NIF (tax identification number). The national incorporation tax Actos Jurídicos Documentados (AJD) is declared and paid using Modelo 600 at the regional tax office; the paid tax copy must be submitted to AEAT together with the deed. Obtain the provisional NIF before proceeding to Mercantile Registry registration.
required_dossiers: First copy of public incorporation deed
Modelo 600 AJD tax declaration and proof of payment
Form 036 (declaración censal) with provisional data
NIE/passport copies of directors and shareholders
Bank certificate and deed of deposit
Notary's certified copy of deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the form 036 is rejected, review the technical refusal from AEAT, correct the requested data, and file again within the same procedure. In case of missing documentation, AEAT may require a longer review period; a new submission is treated as a new application if the deadline expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the deed with the Mercantile Registry and obtain registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial first copy of the deed, the negative name certificate, the provisional NIF, and the evidence of use of the name to the Registry. The registrar must review legality of the deed and corporate governance provisions. If accepted, the registration is noted in the company sheet and the definitive incorporation is recorded. Record the company in the CIRCE system and obtain an executor spreadsheet (hoja de encargo).
required_dossiers: First copy of public deed
Provisional NIF certificate
Negative name certificate
Modelo 600 payment proof
Directors' DNI/NIE copies
Proof of share capital deposit in Spanish credit institution
Certified copy of the deed from the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar enters a notice (defecto) requiring correction, remedy the defect within the given time and file an additional deed supplement. If the notice is maintained, appeal to the Juzgado de lo Mercantil within 2 months; if approved, registration proceeds. Failure to correct can be cured by rectifying the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish incorporation in BORME, register tax definitively and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME), AEAT and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the Registry issues a certificate. BORME publishes the entry automatically from the certificate. Afterwards, the provisional NIF must be converted into a definitive NIF using Form 036 modified within 15 business days. The company must register as an employer and owners must enrol in the relevant social security regime. Also file the company identification with regional tax office if any economic activity tax is applicable.
required_dossiers: Certification of registration from the Mercantile Registry
BORME publication notice
Form 036 modification to definitive NIF and address
Company registration application in social security system (SILTRA)
Bank account proof (for payroll and charges)
Directors' DNI/NIE copies and registration in the corresponding scheme
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BORME publication is delayed, request the Registrar to issue a late publication certificate. If the NIF conversion is not accepted, refile Form 036 with the registration certificate. Social security denial due to incorrect data is cured by correcting employee forms and re-filing within the established deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo through the subordinate industrial department of the Autonomous Community (Consejería de Industria) and, for medical devices, the Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia municipal de actividad clasificada / Licencia de apertura and, where applicable, medical device conformity assessment/authorisation under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) for manufacture/assembly of laparoscopy towers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the environmental authority of the Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B: simplified environmental assessment through the environmental licence procedure (trámite de clasificación) for assembly of electronic medical equipment, unless Annex I size triggers full EIA (then Cat. A, full evaluación de impacto ambiental).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharges to municipal sewer: COD <= 500 mg/L, TSS <= 300 mg/L, pH 6-9, oils <= 120 mg/L. VOC/emissions from cleaning/degreasing operations must remain below the 2 tonnes/year net threshold; if exceeded, solvent management and emission controls under Directive 2010/75/EU apply. Hazardous waste (including electronic circuit residues, spent solvents, contaminated packaging) must be minimised, registered with the regional authority and disposed of through authorised waste managers, with family/lot confirmation for EEE waste under RD 110/2015.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the regional fire brigade in accordance with Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE) DB-SI/DB-SI, including emergency lighting, extinguishers and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate for the building's actual floor loads from cleanroom/robotics equipment; municipal occupancy licence; occupational health and safety evaluation by an accredited mutua, including cleanroom ISO 14644 classification and machine safety compliance with RD 1215/1997 and RD 1644/2002.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its Sede Electrónica portal. The AEAT administers Spanish tax identification, Value Added Tax, Corporate Income Tax, customs and related registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through the AEAT. The incorporation deed and registration details are submitted using Modelo 036, normally initially for a provisional NIF and subsequently for the definitive NIF after registration in the Commercial Registry. The filing must identify the registered office, tax domicile, economic activities, directors, beneficial ownership information where required, and tax representative or attorney-in-fact. A foreign shareholder or foreign corporate director must provide the relevant foreign tax identification details and, where required, obtain a Spanish Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE) or NIF. Foreign corporate documents generally require legalization or apostille and an official Spanish translation unless an applicable treaty or EU documentation rule provides otherwise. The Spanish NIF is also used as the domestic VAT identification number; intra-Community VAT transactions require validation of the number in the VIES system and, where applicable, registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal entity, with worldwide taxation if Spanish tax resident. Available elections or special regimes may include Spanish tax consolidation, the special regime for mergers and other qualifying restructurings, the Canary Islands tax regime where applicable, and other sector-specific regimes subject to statutory conditions and formal elections. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, impose inclusion adjustments or restrict relief for arrangements producing deduction-without-inclusion, double deduction or equivalent mismatches. The entity cannot generally elect transparent pass-through treatment merely by filing a classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), supplemented by customs and certain regional indirect-tax rules applicable in the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None; Spain has no general domestic turnover threshold below which an ordinary business may remain outside VAT registration. A person carrying on an economic activity must generally register and comply with VAT obligations from the commencement of the activity. Separate thresholds and conditions can apply to specific EU small-business, distance-selling and intra-Community regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all taxpayers. Electronic invoicing is mandatory in specified public-sector transactions and is being extended to qualifying private B2B transactions under Law 18/2022, subject to implementing regulations and statutory transition periods. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities with turnover exceeding the statutory threshold, VAT groups and REDEME participants, to transmit prescribed invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT within the applicable deadlines. The Veri*Factu and certified billing-system rules require compliant billing software, integrity and traceability controls, and prescribed transmission or availability features for affected taxpayers under the applicable implementation timetable. There is no general requirement for an AEAT digital stamp or pre-clearance of every invoice. Invoices must contain the statutory data, including issuer and customer identification, VAT number where required, date, sequential number, taxable base, rate, VAT amount and applicable exemption or reverse-charge reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Spain to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT where the Spanish supplier or an authorized customer transports or dispatches the goods and the export is evidenced by customs records and proof of exit from the EU customs territory. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, the supplier satisfies invoicing and EC Sales List reporting requirements, and transport and customer-status evidence are retained. Services may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT or exempt under the place-of-supply rules where supplied to a non-Spanish business customer or otherwise meet the statutory conditions; the result depends on the service category, customer status, place of use and enjoyment, and any applicable special rule. Export zero-rating is not available solely because the customer is non-resident; documentary proof and the applicable place-of-supply or export conditions must be satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Spanish export customs declaration, normally the electronic DUA export declaration and its MRN
Customs confirmation or electronic evidence that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR or equivalent
Purchase order, sales contract and proof linking the exported goods to the Spanish supplier and invoice
Customer VAT identification and intra-Community supply evidence where the transaction is an intra-Community supply rather than an extra-EU export
Proof of payment or foreign inward remittance where commercially or audit-relevant; Spain does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a universal VAT zero-rating document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for qualifying export VAT treatment. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to applicable banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting and foreign-investment reporting rules. If export or intra-Community conditions are not proven, the AEAT may deny the exemption, assess output VAT, recover improperly refunded or deducted input VAT, and charge late-payment interest. Administrative tax penalties depend on the infringement and may generally range from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid or refunded tax, with aggravation or reduction rules. False, incomplete or manipulated customs evidence may also trigger customs sanctions, repayment of customs or VAT benefits and related interest. Deliberate tax fraud can create criminal exposure where the statutory tax-loss thresholds and other elements of a tax offense are met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks, the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the European Central Bank, and the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for foreign-exchange statistical supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full euro convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; no exchange-control authorization is required for current or capital transactions. Dividend and profit remittances from a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted, subject only to corporate income tax filings, transfer-pricing documentation, anti-money-laundering compliance, and mandatory balance-of-payments declarations to the Banco de España where thresholds exceed EUR 50,000 per transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no Spanish statutory export-proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may keep receivables in foreign currency or convert to euro at market rates. Amounts paid or collected from non-residents must be reported to the Banco de España through the official 'Declaración de Transacciones con el Exterior' within the applicable calendar-based statistical deadlines (normally the first twenty days of the month following the transaction for large flows).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with trade finance desk
Capital Escrow Account for non-resident equity injection
Operational Account for payroll and supplier SEPA payments
Capital Escrow Account for shareholders and loan proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2, including Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bnext, can provide EUR IBANs, segregated funds, and low-fee FX conversion, and are supervised by the Banco de España. However, they generally cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, do not offer documentary collections, and are not direct members of TARGET2/SWIFT; they are suitable as a secondary liquidity rail but not as the primary account for ISIC 3250 trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Law 10/2010 on prevention of money laundering, Spanish banks must identify all directors and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, tier-1 banks require at least one signatory director to attend a physical compliance interview at a Spanish branch; remote onboarding via videoconference is occasionally accepted only for EU-residents with certified eID, while non-resident directors must usually appear personally with passport/NIE for certification. Fully virtual account opening for a Spanish SL is uncommon and subject to enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO registered in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction, or ownership chain containing bearer share structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Spanish escritura, certified register of final beneficiaries (Registro de Titularidad Real) issued not more than 3 months prior, organizational charts identifying all individuals with >25% control, passports/NIE of UBOs, sworn source-of-wealth declarations, and a risk assessment from a registered Spanish AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large first inbound transfer for surgical laparoscopy tower production without evident underlying trade contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial agreements with purchase orders, ISIC 3250 manufacturing plant license, ISO 13485 and CE certificates, detailed proforma invoices, list of component suppliers, projected cash flow statement, and a letter of explanation describing the capital injection into the SL's escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or counterparties flagged on PEP, sanctions, or adverse media screenings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Financial Sanctions consolidated list check results, national police certificate of criminal records (certificado de antecedentes penales), legalization and apostille of foreign documentation, favorable legal opinion on the non-application of restrictive measures, and bank-specific enhanced due diligence questionnaire with direct source-of-funds evidence (bank statements and sales ledger).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity inflows must be transferred via SWIFT/SEPA from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's named escrow or operational account in EUR, with the SWIFT field 70 narrative clearly stating 'Capital subscription' and referencing the notarial deed. The SL must classify the transaction under the Bank of Spain balance-of-payments code for direct investment equity (concept 340) and file the electronic declaration unless exempted; the capital increase must also be formalized before a notary and registered in the Registro Mercantil within the statutory period to avoid infraction penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for direct supplier payments, TARGET2/SCT for intra-EU euro settlements, and via UCP 600-compliant commercial letters of credit issued by a Spanish trade-finance bank for Latin American and high-risk transactions. Documentary collections and purchase-order financing may be used in parallel, with each outbound transfer annotated using ISO 20022 purpose codes, e.g., 'TRAD' or 'CGDS', and underlying transport documents retained to prove genuine economic substance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards concluded with authorized Spanish bank counterparties under ISDA 2002 master agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CLP, USD/MXN, and USD/BRL for Latin American revenues faced by the laparoscopy tower exporter
Cross-currency basis swaps for EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm currency pair exposures
European-style vanilla FX options (call/put) purchased for negative-follow-up protection on awarded tenders
Currency swap agreements with non-financial counterparties solely for actual treasury risk hedging, subject to EMIR clearing exemptions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may delay filing and expose directors to liability for statutory non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; for a calendar year-end, normally by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may follow if accounts remain unfiled for one year after the financial year-end, subject to statutory exceptions. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 and may increase for larger companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Central Register of Beneficial Ownership, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts where required; beneficial ownership changes must be reported promptly through the prescribed registry or notarial channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or outdated beneficial ownership information may result in registry defects, filing restrictions, AML enforcement, and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days after six months from the financial year-end; for a calendar year-end, normally 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger fixed filing penalties where no tax is payable, late-payment surcharges, interest, and tax penalties based on the unpaid tax and conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value added tax annual summary, where applicable (Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of January for the preceding calendar year, unless an applicable exemption applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may result in fixed penalties, assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and additional tax sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual information returns for withholding taxes, where applicable (including Modelos 180 and 190)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the first 30 calendar days of January for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate reporting may result in fixed information-return penalties and related withholding tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT, payroll, accounting, and corporate register reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; supporting records available to the Spanish Tax Agency and other competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed after year-end and before annual accounts approval and tax filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Record deficiencies may impair tax deductibility, support tax assessments, and trigger accounting, tax, or director-liability exposure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following limits for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average employees of 50. Audit is also mandatory in certain regulated, public-interest, group, subsidy, or other legally specified circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad). IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated groups and is mandatory for certain listed or regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no universal standalone annual UBO return for every Spanish SL. The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information, report changes through the applicable Commercial Registry or notarial process, and complete the beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts where required. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in ownership and UBO records without undue delay.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700-1,800 per year, depending on registered-office, corporate-secretarial, filing, and resident-representative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-10,000 for a non-complex Spanish SL; higher fees apply for mandatory group, regulated, manufacturing, inventory, or cross-border audit work

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) carrying on an economic activity may benefit from a reduced 15% corporate tax rate for the first two tax periods with positive taxable base, subject to statutory exclusions, loss-offset restrictions and economic substance requirements. Additional reliefs include the participation exemption on qualifying dividends and foreign capital gains, R&D and technological innovation tax credits, export-related deductions, and the investment reserve for certain qualifying assets. All incentives are subject to anti-abuse rules and the substance-over-form doctrine.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Form 200) – Spanish Corporate Income Tax Return; filed exclusively through the AEAT electronic tax portal (Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria) using digital certificate or Cl@ve authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year fiscal year ending 31 December, the statutory deadline is 25 July; for non-calendar fiscal years, the same 25-day rule applies after the six-month anniversary of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF), registered address, dominant economic activity code (CNAE/ISIC 3250), fiscal period, type of return (individual, consolidated, complementaria).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident permanent establishment (PE) must use the Spanish NIF assigned to the PE, enter the PE's Spanish address and report the manufacturing activity under CNAE 3250; a non-resident without a Spanish PE must not submit Form 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 0031–0045 / Accounting Result and Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the statutory accounting profit or loss, then apply permanent and temporary adjustments to reconcile the accounting result with taxable income, including depreciation, provisions, amortisation, valuation adjustments and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must compute profits attributable to the Spanish activity in accordance with Article 13 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS); internal chargebacks from the head office are deductible only if they meet arm's-length substance requirements and are adequately evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 0046–0052 / Tax Base, Loss Offsets and Incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the taxable base before and after offsetting carried-forward tax losses (BIN), available tax credits and incentives, and the reduced new-company rate where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE may offset only those losses that are genuinely attributable to the PE; resident-only incentives such as certain regional credits are not available to non-resident entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 0054–0058 / Quota, Withholdings and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the total corporate tax at 25% or 15% reduced rate, deduct prepayments, withholding tax credits, double-tax relief and any refundable tax credit amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must not use resident-only credits and must reconcile Spain-source income with treaty provisions; excess credits require a tax treaty refund request or Form 210 procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or amount to be refunded, including any late-payment surcharge. Signature field for legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local legal representative must sign electronically with a Spanish digital certificate. Branch profits subsequently remitted to head office are subject to the separate 19% non-resident branch tax unless the remittance is physically prevented by regulatory capital requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 (Form 202) – Corporate Income Tax Instalment Payment (pago fraccionado); submitted via AEAT electronic filing system or the consolidated corporate group form Modelo 220.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Three instalments per fiscal year while using the instalment-prepayment regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, instalments are due within the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the due date is the first 20 days after the relevant instalment period as scheduled in Article 40 LIS and annual AEAT regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate whether the prepayment is calculated on the prior-year taxable base basis (Article 40.2 LIS) or the current-year profit basis for large taxpayers (Article 40.3 LIS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE may use the prior-year basis and must adjust for the company's Spanish-only taxable income; current-year basis may be selected only when the taxpayer has real substance and accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box II / Taxable Base and Extent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the relevant taxable base or positive accounting profit for the instalment period, applying the statutory rate percentage and any deductions authorised for instalment prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the taxable base attributable to the PE excludes non-Spanish activities; if the PE has no permanent establishment in prior periods, a nil or reduced instalment may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report credits and tax prepayments already satisfied in the current period to calculate the net instalment due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits and treaty reliefs are not automatically recalculated for instalments; use only those credits duly substantiated for the Spanish PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay instalments triggers late-payment surcharges of 1% per month, maximum 15%, plus late-payment interest; if AEAT requires payment, enforcement surcharges up to 20% may apply and tax refunds may be suspended. False or unfounded reductions are treated as regular late-payment infractions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for outbound dividends paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder, applied under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime (IRNR). Spanish-resident corporate shareholders may qualify for the participation exemption if holding at least 5% for one year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must supply to the paying SL a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authority, certifying beneficial ownership, and evidence of the qualifying holding period. The payer should apply the reduced treaty rate only after receiving the TRC and must retain the supporting documentation for tax-audit purposes, reporting the payments on Modelo 296. If 19% is withheld incorrectly or excessive withholding occurs, the non-resident may file Modelo 210 to claim a refund, generally within the four-year statute of limitation, attaching the TRC and a certificate of filing by the payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory IRNR withholding rate for both industrial/software royalties and debt interest paid to non-residents is 19%. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, a qualifying associated EU/EEA recipient may be exempt from Spanish withholding on royalties and interest if the beneficial owner holds at least 25% capital for at least 24 months. Under most Spanish DTAs, treaty rates are reduced to between 0% and 10%, with the reduced rate requiring TRC documentation; under the Spain–US DTA, industrial royalties and interest are generally taxed at 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 of annual net turnover triggers the mandatory preparation of the Local File; a Master File is additionally required when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 50,000,000 and the Spanish entity carries out related-party transactions. Related-party transactions below EUR 250,000 may be excluded from detailed documentation in limited cases, but the arm's-length standard always applies to the actual transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substantive economic presence is enforced through the anti-abuse provisions in Article 15 LIS and Article 15 of the Spanish General Tax Law. For a surgical laparoscopy tower manufacturing SL, economic substance is demonstrated through owned production facilities, employed technical staff, assumption of warranty and regulatory-compliant risk, control of inventory and pricing decisions, and actual management functions performed in Spain. Transactions with related Latin American distribution entities are recharacterised when the purported substance does not correspond to the activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating turnover from laparoscopy tower sales through offshore accounts, issuing fictitious invoices to inflate manufacturing costs, or omitting taxable income in excess of EUR 120,000 per tax year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Article 305: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of six times the defrauded amount; administrative penalty under LGT Articles 191 and 193: 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax, plus late-payment interest and loss of tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face joint and several liability for the corporate tax debt under LGT Article 42.2 when they participated negligently in the fraud. Personal civil liability for damages, attachment of bank accounts and personal assets, travel bans and disqualification from benefiting from public aid may be imposed; the corporate veil is pierced when the SL is used as an instrument of concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Absence of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no premises, no employees, no production equipment and no managerial functions while invoicing the manufacture of Ultra-HD 4K laparoscopy towers through Spain solely to exploit treaty exemptions or the reduced new-company rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of income under Article 15 LIS, denial of treaty benefits, retroactive assessment with interest, and penalties for serious infractions under LGT Article 206 including up to 150% of the deficiency and possible cancellation of the NIF registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign backdated minutes, artificial contracts or false declarations may be convicted of false accounting under Criminal Code Article 290; civil liability extends to unpaid corporate tax and social security debt. The court may order disqualification from holding corporate office for up to 15 years and impose travel restrictions where there is a flight risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling surgical laparoscopy towers to a related Latin American distributor at non-arm's-length prices, paying excess management fees or royalties to a low-tax related licensor, or failing to prepare Local/Master File documentation despite surpassing the EUR 10 million turnover threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make an upward transfer pricing adjustment, collect the primary tax liability, apply interest from the original due date, and impose a 15% penalty under Article 18.12 LIS for documentation failure or inaccurate data; where concealment exists, the penalty may reach 150% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign intercompany pricing arrangements without economic analysis face solidary liability for the resulting corporate tax deficiency when their participation is deemed negligent. In severe cases, insolvency-based liability under Ley Concursal and criminal liability for scheme abuse may be pursued; international tax-exposed directors are subject to asset-tracing and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Corruption in Export Medical Equipment Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL as a conduit for payments related to public hospital tenders in Latin America, receiving commissions from shell agents, or executing payments through mule accounts and prepaid instruments to obscure end-customers or public officials.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 for very serious infractions range from EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000, plus confiscation. Criminal conviction for money laundering under Criminal Code Article 301 leads to imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, fines, and forfeiture of the SL's assets; foreign officials bribery raises penalties under Article 445 bis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are exposed to personal criminal proceedings, provisional detention, extradition and travel bans when the Spanish SL is integrated into a transnational corruption scheme. Civil liability includes restitution of laundered proceeds, and courts frequently pierce the corporate veil to satisfy confiscation and compensation orders against the personal assets of the directors.
